title: decentralized-switchback-operator-idempotent-rollback-as-code
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add a Switchback Operator for automated failback workflows, idempotent rollback-as-code Terraform hooks, and Helm lifecycle hooks for evacuation; no breaking changes to existing installer configs.
description:
Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in multi-AZ/on-prem topologies requested an automated, auditable 'switchback' path that performs controlled failover and then a validated failback (switchback) when primary capacity is restored. This PR introduces the Switchback Operator (controller+CRD), idempotent Terraform rollback hooks, Helm lifecycle evacuation hooks, and a runbook-as-code integration for drill automation. Changes include a lightweight controller that orchestrates: preflight validations (consistency/kv-cache sync check), staged evacuations (pod/VM cordon->drain->kv checkpoint), model routing updates via our private control-plane API, and a reversible switchback plan with automatic canary verification. Checklist: - [x] Implement Switchback CRD and controller with leader-election and rate-limited reconciliation - [x] Add helm/templates/evacuate-hook.yaml with post-install/upgrade hooks and pre-delete draining hooks - [x] Provide terraform/modules/hadr/rollback_hook.tf (idempotent, pessimistic locks, state checks) - [x] Add runbooks/hadr/switchback-playbook.yaml as executable playbook for drills - [x] Add e2e-hadr test harness and new unit tests - [x] Add Linear links in code and server logs for observability Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5123/switchback-operator-design, runbook template https://confluence.redwood.ai/hadr/switchback-runbook. Commits: ["a3f4bd1 Add Switchback CRD and controller scaffolding","b9cde88 Implement idempotent terraform rollback hook","d2f0a7e Helm evacuate hooks and templates","e6f98b1 Runbook-as-code and test harness","f1aa554 Fix flakey e2e assertions and improve lock handling"]. High-level changed areas: helm/templates/evacuate-hook.yaml, helm/values.schema.json, helm/Chart.yaml, controller/pkg/switchback/*, terraform/modules/hadr/*, runbooks/hadr/*.yaml, tests/e2e/hadr/*.go, docs/private/hadr.md. Small illustrative snippet: helm/templates/evacuate-hook.yaml (excerpt) "apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: ""{{ include "redwood.fullname" . }}-evacuate""
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
      containers:
      - name: evacuator
        image: ""redwood/hadr-evacuator:0.12.0""
        args: ["--drain","--kv-checkpoint","--wait-canary=3m"]". Rollback semantics: terraform rollback hook is designed to be idempotent and declarative; it acquires a named lock, checks live routing table and kv cache hashes, performs partial rollbacks in stages, and exposes a dry-run mode. Test & CI: initial CI run exposed a flaky e2e test in the orchestration path, fixed in f1aa554; final CI summary below. Operational notes: operator includes metrics (switchback_requests_total, stage_duration_seconds, rollback_errors_total) and structured events go to the private control plane for audit. The runbook-as-code plays nicely with our incident-bot (alerts trigger an actionable link that instantiates a switchback plan). Backwards compatibility: installer values expose optional toggles (hadr.enabled=false by default) so existing installs are unaffected. Migration: small helm values/terraform vars additions documented in docs/private/hadr.md.
